title: Foreword
content:
The University is established primarily for the intellectual, cultural, social and moral development of all students from diverse ethnic, cultural and religious backgrounds. It takes into cognisance the behavioural pattern which characterised students’ lives. It recognises where students are not guided adequately their academic future may be compromised.

This Handbook provides useful information to students of this University especially the newly admitted students so that they might benefit maximally from the rich academic University environment. The Handbook aims at intimating students on how to conduct themselves as members of the University community and the conditions that must guide their conduct throughout their studentship.

The University which is one of the best in Nigeria according to webometrics and the most sought-after university, graduates only those students who have met its requirements in character and learning. The University of Ilorin takes pride of place in maintenance of stable academic calendar. Students should therefore digest every piece of information in this handbook for ignorance of the law is not an excuse.

Being an institution concerned with students’ welfare, a modern library with internet facilities and an enabling learning environment has been provided. There are also recreational centres where students can relax in their leisure time.

Professor Wahab Egbewole, SAN
Vice-Chancellor
June, 2025

title: 1. Preamble
content:
WHEREAS the University of Ilorin (hereinafter referred to as "the University") was established to:

  • Encourage the advancement of learning and to hold out to all persons, without distinction of race, creed, sex, religion, or political conviction, the opportunity of acquiring a higher and liberal education;
  • Provide courses of instruction and other facilities for the pursuit of learning in all its branches, and to make those facilities available on proper terms to such persons as are equipped to benefit from them;
  • Encourage and promote scholarship and conduct research in all fields of learning and human endeavour;
  • Relate its activities to the socio-cultural and economic needs of the people of Nigeria; and
  • Undertake any other activities appropriate for a University of the highest standard.

These objectives would be attainable only in an atmosphere of peace and harmony where the Rule of Law prevails and all students obey and observe all the rules and regulations of the University and display a deep sense of honesty, dedication, dynamism, discipline and respect for constituted authority.

The Senate of the University, in exercise of the powers conferred on it by Section 6(4) of the University of Ilorin Act, CAP 455 Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004, hereby makes the following Rules and Regulations.

IMPORTANT: It is the responsibility of each student not only to acquaint themselves with these Rules and Regulations, but also to always uphold them within or outside the University since the University degree is awarded to students found worthy both in character and learning.

title: 2. Students' Conduct
content:
The University is established primarily for the development of students intellectually, socially and culturally. It also aims at inculcating good character as an integral part of education.

An acceptance of admission offer by a student into the University and swearing to Matriculation Oath automatically implies that he or she has accepted to abide by the Rules and Regulations that may from time to time be made for the governance of the University.

Such acceptance also carries with it an obligation that the student shall conduct himself or herself as a law-abiding and responsible member of the academic community in accordance with the University's best standards, rules and other conditions established by the legally constituted authorities.

Ignorance of the rules shall NOT be a defence. All students are required to familiarise themselves with this handbook.

title: 3. Personal and Academic Integrity
content:
Any act of dishonesty of any kind is a behavioural issue which must be avoided. Minimum standards:

  1. Be honest and conduct himself/herself in an ethical manner in the pursuit of his/her studies;
  2. Attend all lectures punctually and be properly dressed in accordance with acceptable dress code;
  3. Maintain high degree of orderliness and decorum in the class and lecture room;
  4. Honestly complete and submit assignments as when due;
  5. Cite references correctly in assignments;
  6. Maintain ethical standards of the Library while carrying out assignments/researches;
  7. Cooperate, if called upon, in the investigation of any allegation of dishonesty;
  8. Take pride in upholding the ethical standards through words, writing, attitude and behaviour;
  9. Regard other members of the University community as part of a family and live harmoniously;
  10. Maintain good personal hygiene. Hostel rooms should be as clean as possible;
  11. Dress decently in compliance with dress code;
  12. No involvement in pornography either within or outside the University;
  13. Avoid: promiscuity, cheating, conflict of interest, plagiarism, fabrication, unauthorised aids, falsification, impersonation.

Every student is required to maintain high standard of integrity. The University regards as serious offences any act of unethical, immoral, dishonest, disloyal or destructive behaviour.

title: 4. Disciplinary Rules
content:
Rules of discipline require that a student shall:

  • a. Not engage in any activity which interferes with University objectives, others' activities, rights of persons lawfully present, teaching/research, Council/Senate business, administration, or official duties.
  • c. Not steal, destroy, damage, deface, vandalise or take unauthorised possession of University property.
  • d. Not paste posters indiscriminately except at designated areas.
  • e. Not simulate, forge, falsify, misuse, alter, damage or destroy any University record/document (written, printed, magnetic, electronic, photographic).
  • f. Not impersonate any officer or employee.
  • g. Not do anything negatively affecting University or members.
  • h. Not involve in: Character defamation, Stealing, Illegal drug possession/use/abuse, Destruction of properties, Unauthorised posting on Social Media, Blackmailing.
  • i. Not disrespect any official performing official assignment.
  • j. Not write insulting letter to an official.
  • k. Not bypass official line of communication. Approved line: HOD → Dean of Faculty. Student grievances (non-academic) through Dean of Student Affairs. Students' Union correspondence must be signed by President and Secretary and routed through DSA.
  • l. Not without approval, communicate with external agencies/governments for financial sponsorship/aid.
  • m. Not be in possession of dangerous objects.

Any student invited to Student Disciplinary Committee (SDC) and fails to honour invitation 3 times shall be deemed guilty as charged. Decisions communicated through HOD and/or pasting in conspicuous designated areas.

title: 5. Appeal Against Decisions
content:
1. In all disciplinary cases, student has right to appeal to Council through HOD, Dean, VC against recommendation of SDC ratified by Administration within 48 days of receipt of disciplinary decision.
  2. Appeals considered by Council through independent Committee of Council which shall make appropriate recommendation to Council.

title: 6. Halls of Residence
content:
a. Accommodation

  • Due to limited bedspaces, accommodation provided to eligible students through online balloting. Fees as approved and advertised. Private hostels available.
  • Modalities determined by Dean of Student Affairs.
  • No accommodation except student is in good standing and duly registered.
  • Expelled students automatically ejected without refund.
  • Responsible for cleaning rooms and laundry, making beds, participating in sanitation.
  • Merchandising prohibited in hostels.

b. Exeat

  • Must obtain exeat from Hall Masters/Mistresses before leaving campus.
  • Emergency: leave written statement with Porters indicating destination, reasons, duration. Porters report immediately to Student Affairs Unit.

c. Visit to Hall

Visitors received in Common Room only.

d. Approved Hall Functions

  • Permission for use of grounds/common rooms/notice boards from Dean via Hall Masters, 48hrs notice.
  • Meetings/parties: written approval required. Parties only in Common Room, not beyond 8pm. Only water & soft drinks allowed. No alcohol/drugs.

e. Electrical Appliances

  • No boiling rings, freezers, heating coils, hot plates, multiple outlets etc. Rechargeable/solar lamps allowed, not candles during outage.

f-k. Other Rules

  • Smoking/Sales: Sales and smoking strictly prohibited anywhere on campus.
  • Fighting: Prohibited. Provocation without retaliation still leads to SDC.
  • Pets: Prohibited - dogs, cats, fish, rabbits, tortoise, chameleons, chickens, cows, horses, birds, reptiles etc.
  • Squatting: No student in room not allocated to him/her.
  • Security: Lock doors, remove keys, deposit keys with porters during vacations. University not responsible for loss.
  • Parking: Cars/motorcycles/bicycles must be registered with Student Affairs Unit, parked at designated places at owner's risk.

title: 7. Catering Services
content:
Catering provided on campus by private caterers - Canteens and Eateries. Students pay for what they consume and must comply with regulations as formulated.

Anti-social behaviour in and around canteens, eateries and campus is frowned at.

title: 8. Orientation of Fresh Students
content:
Orientation takes place first few weeks of resumption. Organised by Student Affairs Unit in collaboration with other units to enlighten about academic, social, security, policies, library, sports, counselling, transport, medical services and campus integration.

Opportunity to familiarise with rules, regulations, procedures, and meet Registrar, Dean of Student Affairs, Deans, HODs, Senior Officers.

All newly admitted students must attend ALL orientation activities and sign attendance register.

title: 9. Registration of Students
content:
Newly admitted students commence registration per University guidelines. Clinic registration is prerequisite for complete registration.

Presentation of Names: Maximum 3 names including surname, surname first in capitals, then other names e.g. AFUYE, Moses Olarinde.

title: 10. University Health Services
content:
Available Services

  • Medical examination at point of entry for newly admitted.
  • Laboratory: blood, urine, stool analysis.
  • Curative services as Primary Health Care Centre.
  • Emergency services 24 hours.
  • Referral to other institutions such as UITH when required.
  • Environmental Health: Hostel inspection, pest control, Health Education for food handlers.

Important Notice

Student Medical Examination and Registration is mandatory for:

  • Make-Up Tests and Examination
  • Treatment at University Health Services Unit
  • Final year clearance before NYSC mobilisation
No medical report/certificate from outside University Health Services shall be countenanced until duly certified by Director of Health Services.

title: 11. Matriculation, Numbers & Identity Card
content:
a. Matriculation

Only students who satisfied minimum admission requirements are matriculated. Each swears to Matriculation Oath (Appendix C). Violation is very serious offence.

b. Matriculation Number

  • Assigned upon registration. No official document valid without it.
  • No previously matriculated student should matriculate second time.
  • Must not produce/reproduce another student's or non-existing number as own.

c. Identity Cards

  • Issued upon matriculation, valid for period indicated, renewable. Must be worn with faculty branded lanyard on neck at all times on campus.
  • Required for Library, Lecture Rooms, Exam Venues, Administrative Building, Counselling Centre, Student Affairs, Labs, Hall etc.
  • Loss: Report in writing to Deputy Registrar (Examinations & Records) via Level Adviser → HOD → Dean. Application for new card endorsed by Security Unit and DSA with Police Report and Affidavit. Fee determined by University. Temporary ID by Faculty Officer after compliance.
  • Submission: On leaving University (completion, relocation, transfer, misconduct) must return ID to Deputy Registrar via Faculty Officer or DSA.
  • Misuse: Offence to misuse own or other students' ID by transfer or impersonation.

title: 12. University Library
content:
Locations: Main Library, Law Library, e-Library within main campus and College of Health Sciences Library. Open to students upon proper registration.

DayHours
Monday - Friday8:00am - 8:00pm
Saturday8:00am - 1:00pm
Sunday6:00pm - 8:00pm
National/State Environmental Saturday10:00am - 3:00pm

Closed on Public Holidays. Librarian may extend hours during exams - currently 24 hours around examination periods.

title: 13. Intra-Campus Transport
content: Intra & inter campus services: buses, korope (mini-bus), tricycle (keke napep). Subsidised fare fixed by University. Must be duly registered, follow approved routes, halt operation at 12 midnight.

title: 14. Regulations Governing Conduct of Exams
content:
A. Eligibility

All duly registered students eligible except:

  • Absent >6 weeks in any semester without permission → deemed voluntarily withdrawn.
  • Fails to attend up to 75% practical/lecture hours.
  • MB;BS and related: No PA score or incomplete clinical posting ineligible. PA based on periodic tests (200/300 levels) and evaluation during clinical years by supervisors and end-of-posting exams at 400/500/600 levels.

B. Instructions to Students

  1. Acquaint with exam regulations.
  2. Attend punctually. Arrival >30 mins after start not admitted.
  3. Bring own ink, pens, rulers, etc. Prohibited: lecture notes, textbooks, jotters, bags, mobile phones, wristwatches, related items. Venue includes hall and surroundings.
  4. Sign attendance register at beginning.
  5. Having signed, must not leave without submitting script.
  6. Do not leave for any reason without informing invigilator.
  7. Keep to sitting arrangement, no removal of chairs. Revision outside hall only.
  8. Communication among students prohibited.
  9. Silence observed; attract invigilator by raising hand.
  10. No scrap paper, writing/jotting on question paper. Rough work in answer booklet and crossed. Supplementary sheets not supplied until 30 mins after commencement, attached even if only rough work.
  11. Mathematics/Engineering Drawing: bring own instruments (compass, dividers, protractors, set squares). Personal copies of Mathematical/Statistical Tables allowed if no inscriptions.
  12. Before submission, ensure matric number and question numbers inserted. Not allowed to remove/mutilate any paper/material supplied.
  13. Use matriculation numbers for examinations.
  14. Not allowed to submit scripts in first 30 mins and last 15 mins.
  15. Remain seated while invigilators collect scripts.
  16. Write names, matric numbers, department and sign attendance sheet.
  17. Calculators: non-programmable only, small hand-held battery/solar, no borrowing, no manuals/packets, switch off and blank memory on entry, one per student, available for inspection. Contravention = misconduct.

title: 15. Examination Code of Conduct, Offences & Penalties
content:
i. Code of Conduct - Students shall:

  • Not introduce/attempt to introduce hand bags, books, notes, mobile phones, electronic devices, i-pad/i-pod, flash drives, storage devices, prohibited aids.
  • Not enter venue with inscriptions on dress/body whether relevant or not.
  • Not pass/attempt to pass information between persons.
  • Not act in collusion, copy or attempt to copy.
  • Only use matriculation numbers (no names).
  • Not leave until 50% of time allocated expires.
  • Not write exam for another, nor have another write for them.
  • Not be in possession of incriminating materials either used or not, including impersonation before/during/after exam.
  • CBT exams: be orderly and abide by centre guidelines.

ii. Procedure for Investigating Alleged Misconduct

  1. Student caught must sign and submit written statement to Chief Invigilator in hall. Failure = admission of charge.
  2. Chief Invigilator reports to Dean through Faculty Exam Coordinator (Sub-Dean) immediately after exam, not later than 12 hours.
  3. Dean within 48 hours sets up panel of not less than 3 academic staff to investigate. Report to Registrar within 2 weeks; Registrar determines whether matter goes to SDC.
  4. SDC within 4 weeks investigates and recommends penalty to Vice-Chancellor per Section 18 of University Act.

iii. Penalties

If student sits for course not registered for, no score recorded.

D. Examination Leakage

Where Dean believes question/paper content known before date/time to persons other than authorised, he may order suspension/cancellation/setting new questions. Investigate and report to VC.

E. Absence from Examination

  • Must present for registered examinations. Failure for reasons other than proven ill-health, accident, proven emergencies = deemed failed. Misreading timetable not acceptable.
  • Ill during exam period: report in writing to Dean via HOD and/or Health Services.

F. Make-Up Examinations

Specially arranged for students who could not sit normal exams due to ill-health or unavoidable circumstances, treated on merit.

  • Absent on account of ill-health confirmed by Director of Health Services may be given make-up based on Senate guidelines or take next available regular exam.
  • Recommendation by Faculty Board provided ill-health reported to Dean via HOD and student obtained written report from Director dated prior to end of exam or evidence of hospitalisation during exam period.
  • Normally conducted within 3 weeks and concluded not later than 5 weeks of following semester.

G. Determination of Result

  • Deemed passed if satisfied Senate in all requirements (including GNS & GSE). Referred students deemed passed when fulfilled.
  • Pass Mark: 40% all Faculties except Vet Medicine, Pharmaceutical Sciences, MB;BS, Medical Lab Sciences, B.NSc, Doctor of Optometry where 50%.
  • Make-up: updated good-standing result processed through Deputy Registrar (Academic Support Services) to Senate within first 5 weeks of new semester.
  • Result Verification: Student completes online Result Verification Form, submits to HOD for transmission to Deputy Registrar. HOD within one week issues verified result confirming old or new score, copy to Deputy Registrar. If review occurs, HOD gives reasons and forwards Verification Report through Dean to Director Academic Planning and Deputy Registrar. If still not satisfied, obtain Re-mark Request Form from Deputy Registrar.

title: 16. Students' Clubs and Organisations
content:
a. Recognition

  • Submit prescribed completed Application Forms to Dean, Student Affairs.
  • Letters of undertaking from staff Adviser/Patron.
  • Objectives and constitution in agreement with University objectives.
  • Renew registration each session.
  • Writers' Clubs, magazines/journals, writers/columnists must be registered and approval obtained before publication.
  • Change of name requires approval.
  • Approval for any programme before commencement.
  • Expected affiliated to Students' Union.
  • Events outside campus must obtain security approval.
  • Excursion visits require DSA approval.

b. Guests from Outside University

Freedom of enquiry allowed but protocol required. For President, Governor, Minister, Commissioner, Head of Diplomatic Mission or other dignitaries, inform Dean in writing and obtain approval at least 4 weeks before invitation.

c. Guidelines for Campus Media & Journalism

  • No Media organisation operates as Campus Media unless duly registered with SAU with written document.
  • Freelance campus Journalist must register real names, aliases, pen names, credentials with SAU.
  • Group wishing to operate as freelance Journalist/Writers Club/Media Organisation must comply with Handbook.
  • Every registered Media Organisation/Writers Club shall have Editorial Board (min 2 members) registered every session.
  • Duty to verify veracity before publishing.
  • Six copies of any journal/magazine/write-up deposited with Dean before/at release, receipt acknowledged.
  • Members individually and collectively responsible for malicious, false, libelous publications within or outside campus concerning staff, students, or group.
  • Freelance journalist solely responsible for false/libelous publication.
  • No Press Organisation shall direct libelous/injurious article to staff, students, groups.

d. Final Year Sign-Out Regulations

Student should NOT:

  • Engage in noisy disturbing activities (DJ, drums, trumpeting, loud instruments) around admin/academic environment.
  • Involve in reckless driving alone or in convoy.
  • Inscription on fellow student dress, pour water/liquid in name of celebration.

Wears with student names at back and old school dressing not prohibited as long as dress-code not violated.

title: 17. Religious Activities
content:
• Free to belong to religious organisations per Sections 38 and 40 of Constitution of FRN 1999 as amended guaranteeing freedom of religion.
  • No sermon/witnessing in unauthorised places: cafeteria, canteen, eateries, hostels, lecture rooms, theatres, library, buses, vehicles, car parks etc.
  • Room to room and within room preaching/witnessing not allowed in hostels.
  • Free to use University facilities after prior permission.
  • Free to use designated facilities for religious activities but not academic facilities like lecture theatres, classrooms, laboratories. Permission in writing from DSA.
  • Applications forwarded to appropriate organ; approval from SAU required.
  • Public address system forbidden except authorised worship centres like Chapel Building for Sunday Service and Mosques for Friday Jumat Service.
  • Not allowed to paste/display religious or any banners/posters/literature/stickers anywhere without written permission of DSA.
  • University has precedence in use of all its facilities.

title: 18. Demonstration and Protest
content:
University recognises open communication and dialogue, and legitimate rights to dissent, disagree, hold different opinion as integral to academic freedom. Regulations:

  • Give advance notice to Dean of Student Affairs at least 7 days about place, nature, methods, date, time of commencement.
  • Shall not use University property for any demonstration.
  • When on campus, University reserves right to use legitimate means to protect life and property.
  • Before outside campus demonstration, obtain Police clearance and security on own, like other citizens, responsible for own action.
  • For lecture-free day in commemoration of yearly celebrations, give at least 2 weeks notice to DSA. University reserves right to approve/disapprove.
  • No violent protests condoned; violators face consequences.

title: 19. Anti-Social Activities
content:
a. Possession of Dangerous Weapons

Guns, knives, daggers, swords, grenades, acid etc forbidden in hostel or around premises. Caught → SDC.

b. Secret Societies

Definition: Organisation/group/confraternity whose activities, inner functions, membership concealed. Proscribed by University in 1978 and FG in 1979. Remains firmly proscribed.

Includes any association of 2+ persons whose aims not publicly disclosed/registered/made known to University Authorities; whose activities manifest secrecy, mysticism, perversion, coercion, violence, fraud, immorality, drunkenness, lawlessness and related anti-social behaviour.

Found identifying/belonging/operating/canvassing/participating/associating with secret society/unregistered association within/outside Unilorin → SDC.

c. Public Disturbance

Source of sounds unreasonably disturbing/interferes peace/comfort/endangers safety/health. No noisy disturbing activities (drums, trumpeting, musical instruments) around admin/academic environment without permission. No reckless driving alone or in convoy.

Generally students are peace-loving. University through ambience of regulations shall deal with misconduct; criminality handed to Police. Public disturbance = unlawful act/omission endangering public safety/health/comfort per Nigerian law.

title: 20. Dress Code
content:
All students reminded there is a DRESS CODE which must be observed at all times. University impacts positively intellectually and morally in pursuit of TOTAL BEING. Degrees awarded only to deserving students worthy in learning and character.

A. Male Students

  1. Hair neat and well combed at all times
  2. Not coloured (except natural)
  3. Well kept and groomed
  4. Haircuts not carry inscriptions
  5. Curled hair not acceptable
  6. Artificial dread locks, plaiting, weaving or braiding not acceptable
  7. Beards well kept

B. Female Students

  1. Weaving, plaiting, braiding, fixing and wigs acceptable
  2. Hair extensions with colours Blue, Green, White, Yellow, Red, Pink, Purple or combination not acceptable
  3. Hair neatly packed and weaved
  4. Hairstyle not carry inscriptions
  5. All wears below knee level
  6. Pencil trousers allowed but must complement with tops covering butt line
  7. Traditional/corporate wears that do not reveal sensitive parts acceptable

EVERY STUDENT MUST HANG STUDENT I.D. CARD ON NECK.

C. Unacceptable Wears (Lecture Halls, Library, Labs, Exam Venues, Seminar Rooms, Faculties, Administrative building, University vehicles)

  1. Dress exposing sensitive parts: cleavage, chest, back, navel, thigh, armpit (sleeveless/half sleeves revealing armpits)
  2. Tight fitting wears
  3. Transparent/see through
  4. Tattered/Ripped Jeans
  5. T-shirts with obscene inscriptions depicting immorality, hooliganism, cultism
  6. Indelible markings and body tattoos by male students
  7. Leggings/Jeggings with short top
  8. Skimpy: Spaghetti, Camisole only, body hugs, topless blouse, shorts
  9. Knickers
  10. Bathroom slippers not acceptable within admin/academic areas
  11. Heavy make-ups
  12. Sagging trousers
  13. Wearing earrings by male students
  14. Rumpled and dirty clothes
  15. Skin/ear piercing by male students
  16. Dread, Galax, Fadeout and Rough Coil Haircuts, Unkempt Appearance
  17. Hair plaiting/weaving by male students

Collection can be seen in Appendix B. Some Faculties/Departments have prescribed Dress Codes - comply.

D. Penalty

Violation is serious misconduct attracting strong warning by DSA and/or appearance before SDC if consistent.

THE WAY YOU DRESS DETERMINES THE WAY YOU ARE ADDRESSED

title: 21. Sexual Assault & Harassment Reporting
content:
Definition

Non-consensual sexual activity ranging from unwanted touching to rape, unsolicited sexual advances, verbal and non-verbal conducts that forcefully or subtly lure student into sexual relationship.

1. Non-Verbal

  • Unwanted suggestive gestures, Leering, Displaying sexually explicit images, Stalking

2. Physical

  • Inordinate affection towards opposite sex and unwanted physical contact: touching, forceful kissing, groping, pecking, fondling, assault
  • Sexual violence showing physical aggression/harm for sex
  • Use of authority to coerce student for sexual gain
  • Rape/sexual assault

3. Cyber

  • Cyber sexual bullying: sexual comments, blackmails, use of nudity, threats/taunts to intimidate/harass via social media
  • Watching pornography on campus
  • Sending nude pictures to others

Reporting Channels

Report to:

  • Dean of Faculty
  • Head of Department
  • Dean of Student Affairs
  • Director, Unilorin Counselling and Human Development Centres

Channels:

  • Direct to Vice-Chancellor
  • Dress Code Committee
  • Trusted confidant

title: 22. Use of Student Union Building (SUB)
content:
SUB and Common Rooms are relaxation centres. Rules:

  • No smoking in building or premises.
  • Gambling in whatever form prohibited in campuses including SUB, Common rooms, Halls.
  • Not permitted to turn SUB or offices to place of abode.

Violation = misconduct liable to disciplinary action.

title: 23. Counselling and Human Development Centres
content:
To prevent rise in anti-social activities and encourage positive thinking and total well-being, University provides professional Counsellors housed in Centre and Annex offices located on Main Campus, Mini Campus, College of Health Sciences and School of Preliminary Studies. Counsellors assigned to each Faculty. Students encouraged to consult frequently for guidance on personal, academic, socio-personal life.

Services:

  • Educational/Academic Counselling
  • Career and Vocational Counselling
  • Personal-Social Counselling
  • Marriage and Family Counselling
  • Health Counselling
  • Research and Other Related Activities
  • Individual and group counselling
  • Behavioural management
  • Human Development and life skills training

title: 24. Recreational Centres
content:
Available:

  • Unilorin Zoological Garden
  • University Stadium
  • Unilorin Lakeside Resort
  • Kwara State Stadium
  • Flower Garden
  • Owu Falls, Palms Shopping Mall, Diamond Park, Succoth Valley Garden, Sobi Hill, Ilorin Gulf Club etc.

title: 25. Sanctions for Violation
content:
• Fines: DSA and Hall Masters/Mistresses may impose implementable fines (Appendix A) for offences in Halls. Failure to pay within 7 days → SDC.
  • Restitution: Pay for damage/loss/misappropriation of University or members' property.
  • Reprimand/Warning: Recorded; considered in future breaches.
  • Suspension/Rustication: Withdraw for stated period, comply with conditions.
  • Expulsion: Ceases to be member, loses all rights/privileges, may require compensation.

title: 26. Conclusion
content:
If any misconduct not captured by Handbook, SDC may exercise discretion to apportion appropriate sanctions considering circumstances.

Violations by student(s), Students' Union Executive, Organisations/clubs or individuals may lead to fine, restitution, reprimand/warning, suspension/rustication or expulsion plus other measures deemed appropriate.

Students should sustain confidence reposed in them by adhering strictly to Rules and Regulations thereby propagating good name of University of Ilorin.

We wish you a successful stay.

title: Appendix B: Dress Code Examples
content:
Appendix B contains pictorial examples from original handbook:

  • Acceptable: Corporate/traditional wears below knee that do not reveal sensitive parts, neatly packed hair, faculty ID lanyard, pencil trousers with tops covering butt line, neat grooming.
  • Unacceptable: Transparent, tight-fitting, tattered jeans, spaghetti/camisole, leggings with short top, sagging, heavy makeup, bathroom slippers in academic areas, tattoos (male), earrings/braids (male), coloured hair extensions (blue/green/white/yellow/red/pink/purple), dread/galax/fadeout rough coil, rumpled dirty clothes, exposure of cleavage/chest/back/navel/thigh/armpit.

Refer to pages 48-49 of original PDF for images. University enforces strictly at Lecture Halls, Library, Laboratories, Examination Venues, Faculties, Administrative buildings and University vehicles.

title: Appendix C: Matriculation Oath
content:
1. I have not previously matriculated in this University;
  2. I will pay due respect and obedience to authorities of University of Ilorin and faithfully observe all regulations which may from time to time be issued for good administration, including directive that students make restitution for damage done to University or public property whether in course of protest or otherwise;
  3. I will obey and observe all University rules and regulations, and display deep sense of honesty, dedication, dynamism, discipline and respect for constituted authority.
  4. I am not a secret cult member;
  5. I will not either alone, or in conjunction with other students, engage in any acts of violence, or other improper conduct, or in acts calculated to damage property of University or community;
  6. During period of my stay, I shall not belong to any secret cult and shall not in any way aid or abet cultism or fail to disclose to authorities or police identity of cultist(s) or activities which come to my knowledge;
  7. I will not participate in any activity of, or belong to any student Organisation, whether on campus or not, unless I have evidence that Organisation is duly registered with University as at time of activity/membership.
  8. I have not registered for, neither will I register for, or undertake any other course of study either full-time or part-time in this or any other Institution during period of my studentship.
  9. In case of breach of any clause, Vice-Chancellor has sole prerogative to summarily expel me;
  10. My parents/Guardians have guaranteed my resolve to abide by this declaration made bonafide; and
  11. I make this Oath truthfully, in accordance with Oaths Act.
